title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-21
lineage: Sony dynamic mics (balcony, 20' spread) > Sony 124 Cassette Deck > Norelco 120 normal bias tape > Susie Q > Tascam 122mk3 > Lucid ADA1000 A/D Converter > Tascam CDRW700 > EAC > Soundforge > CD Wave > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: A gritty but surprisingly clear audience tape captures an early‑1970 show that bursts with energy, highlighted by a scorching Viola Lee Blues and the rare Seven jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience source from March 21, 1970 that, despite some vintage tape roughness, sounds remarkably clear for its era. The performance is consistently praised – especially the blistering Viola Lee Blues, Walkin’ the Dog, and the uncommon Seven/Cumberland jams – and Jerry’s guitar work is described as primal and intense. Overall fans regard this show as a magical snapshot of the Dead’s early‑70 vibe.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and highlight both strong musical moments and acceptable (good) recording quality; the weight of positive comments yields a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape with vintage grit but surprisingly clear mids and highs; occasional roughness noted, yet captures the live atmosphere well.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑show set flows informally with high energy; rare jams (Seven, Cumberland) are interspersed with crowd‑pleasers like Viola Lee Blues and Walkin' the Dog, creating a dynamic and engaging progression.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for intense, primal psychedelic blues guitar work and deep tone.
